Ganesha. The elephant-headed god of beginnings, wisdom, and the remover of obstacles in Hindu tradition.

Ganesha is the son of Shiva and Parvati, the divine couple of the Hindu pantheon. He is one of the most widely worshipped deities across India and beloved across all branches of Hinduism. He is worshipped before undertaking any significant endeavor, representing intelligence, prudence, and the clearing of hindrances on the path to success.

He is depicted with an elephant's head and a human body, embodying both earthly strength and divine wisdom in a single form. Ganesha carries a modak, a sweet dumpling, a goad, and a noose. These symbolize prosperity, discipline, and the binding of desires. He is known as the remover of obstacles, the vighnaharta, and is invoked at the beginning of rituals, ceremonies, and new ventures for blessings and success.

Ganesha is associated with intelligence, cunning, and the written word. He is worshipped by scholars, artists, and those seeking knowledge. His vahana, his mount, is a mouse or rat, representing humility and the ability to navigate even the smallest spaces.

One of the most recognizable deities in the world due to his distinctive elephant head, Ganesha has become a symbol of Hinduism globally. His teachings emphasize that obstacles are gateways to growth, showing that wisdom lies in transcending rather than avoiding challenges.
